extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, peer reviewers, clinical researchers, medical educators and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and arguments for designing specialization, training, appraisal and standards for peer reviewers of randomized controlled trials (RCTs), including selection criteria, curricular content, and mechanisms to signal review quality to readers. Focused on clinical/medical journals and stakeholders who set peer review policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT adherence for RCT reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The CONSORT statement: specifies in detail how randomized controlled trials should be reported to improve transparency and help peer reviewers and readers make informed judgements about clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CONSORT as the reporting standard for RCT manuscripts; evidence (Cochrane review and other studies) indicates CONSORT improves completeness of reporting and thereby aids peer review. The article recommends CONSORT could form the framework for training peer reviewers of RCTs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialization of peer review for RCTs
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce specialization so that peer review for randomized controlled trials is done by individuals with defined training, ongoing appraisal and revalidation specific to RCT methodology and reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialization allows fields to define aims/purposes of peer review appropriate to their needs; trained RCT peer reviewers could review across existing peer review models and enable a consistent baseline of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training curriculum and competencies for RCT peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewer training content should define the knowledge and skills needed to appraise an RCT critically, including spotting fundamental methodological and reporting flaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CONSORT could be the backbone of training content. Training should cover trial design, methods, trial registration, reporting guidelines, and ability to detect errors and inappropriate revisions. The literature shows many reviewers lack understanding of reporting guidelines and often fail to detect deliberately introduced errors, so training must address these gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic evaluation, appraisal and revalidation of peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should undergo ongoing appraisal and periodic revalidation to ensure retained competence in critically appraising RCTs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reviewer performance can decline or be inadequate despite training, periodic assessment and revalidation (like other professional skills affecting patient care) are recommended to maintain standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of peer review as a professional skill with measurable standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review (of RCTs) should be recognized as a professional skill with measurable standards that are independent of the journal or publisher business model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separating standards from commercial considerations gives reviewers recognition, enables consistent selection by editors, allows publishers to innovate while maintaining baseline quality, and sets a platform for research on peer review effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance symbol/kitemark for RCTs
rubrics_metrics.description: A searchable 'quality assurance' symbol or label should be attached to RCTs (and their peer review reports when public) that have been reviewed by at least one appropriately trained and accredited expert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to the BSI Kitemark, such a symbol would help lay people and clinicians identify studies reviewed by trained specialists and could be applied across peer review models (open/closed, pre/post-publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training should begin early and be ongoing
rubrics_metrics.description: Training in peer review should begin in medical schools and continue throughout professional life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because informal learning late in career may be ineffective, early introduction of peer review skills in curricula plus ongoing education can build necessary competencies before researchers begin reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus definition of aims, standards and training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Major stakeholders (medical schools, regulatory/accreditation bodies, funders, publishers, editors and lay representatives) should reach consensus on the definition, purpose, standards and training requirements for peer review of RCTs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A consensus is needed to define what peer review should achieve in clinical research and to operationalize training, accreditation and the proposed quality-assurance mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, consistent selection criteria for peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and journals should adopt clear and consistent eligibility criteria for selecting peer reviewers, rather than highly variable, journal-specific practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Currently journal instructions and eligibility criteria vary; consistent criteria (independent of business model) would help editors choose appropriate reviewers and help ensure baseline competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubriq eligibility criteria for reviewers (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubriq requires peer reviewers to have a terminal degree in the area of interest; be employed full time in an accredited research university at professor/instructor/postdoc/faculty research associate level; be a published first or corresponding author in a peer reviewed journal within the last four years; and have prior experience as a journal peer reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubriq also uses a standardized scorecard to evaluate manuscripts. This is presented as an example of explicit, stringent eligibility and standardized evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peerage of Science eligibility and validation (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peerage of Science validates reviewers as scientists who have published a peer reviewed scientific article as first or corresponding author in an established international journal; reviewers select manuscripts they wish to review and peer review reports are reviewed by fellow reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This model emphasizes peer validation and reviewer self-selection informed by publication track record.

rubrics_metrics.name: F1000Research author-suggested referee guidance (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: F1000Research asks authors to identify five potential referees; suggested referees should not have collaborated with the authors in the past five years, be from the same institution, or be too senior to undertake such refereeing; they should ideally have authored at least one article in the field as the lead author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an example of operational constraints on selecting referees to reduce conflicts of interest and ensure field-relevant expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and mandate use of reporting guidelines by reviewers and journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers and journals should be encouraged (or required) to use reporting guidelines (e.g., CONSORT) when assessing manuscripts because many reviewers currently lack understanding of these guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys show inconsistent journal guidance and lack of reviewer awareness; improving uptake of reporting guidelines would improve reporting completeness and peer review effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define field-specific aims of peer review instead of one-size-fits-all
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than attempting a single universal aim for peer review across all fields and study designs, define the aims of peer review specific to disciplines and study designs (e.g., clinical RCTs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specialized approach is more manageable and allows training and standards to be targeted to the needs of different research types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make peer review measurable to enable research on effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish baseline measurable standards for peer review so that future research can evaluate the effectiveness and quality of peer review and compare different peer review innovations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having measurable standards and accredited reviewers permits comparative studies of peer review models and assessments of whether training or innovations improve detection of errors and reporting quality.
